candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — controlled-substance discrepancy recognition
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize DEA-listed factors used to evaluate significant controlled-substance losses, including repeated loss patterns, randomness, and efforts to resolve discrepancies.

options.A: Whether the missing medication was a brand-name rather than a generic product.
options.B: Whether there is a pattern of losses over time, whether the losses appear random, and what efforts have been made to resolve them.
options.C: Whether the discrepancy occurred during a day shift rather than a night shift.
options.D: Whether the employee involved has worked at the facility for more than one year.

candidate.rationale: DEA's Theft or Loss guidance lists several factors for determining whether a controlled-substance loss is significant, including a pattern of losses over a specific time period, whether losses appear random, and the results of efforts to resolve them. Therefore B is correct. DEA also considers the quantity and specific substance lost, association with access by specific individuals or unique activities, diversion potential, and local trends. The brand/generic status, work shift, and employee tenure in A, C, and D are not listed as significance factors in this guidance.
candidate.source_claim_supported: DEA identifies patterns of controlled-substance losses over time, randomness, and efforts to resolve the losses as factors in determining whether a loss is significant, along with quantity, substance, access association, diversion potential, and local trends.
